tasks.body:
The index is rebuilt in full far more often than the work justifies. Two
independent causes, both in `createProjectIndexStore` (`src/modules/records/index.ts:449`).

**The TTL is 1000 ms.** `maxAgeMs` defaults to 1000 and neither caller overrides it —
`src/server/http.ts:255` constructs the store with no options, `src/modules/mcp/server.ts`
uses `options.indexMaxAgeMs || 1000`. `loadedAt` is stamped *after* the build finishes, so
the useful window is one second of wall clock. Any second interaction that involves a human
pausing to think arrives outside it. Measured against the running HTTP server after the
walk fix: first request 1 016 ms, immediate repeat 116 ms, and a repeat 1.2 s later 822 ms.
Before the walk fix the same pattern cost ~6.6 s every time, which is what made the local
UI feel broken.

**`invalidate()` drops everything.** It sets `cached = null`, and there is no per-domain
granularity — `buildProjectIndex` loads cards, docs, changelog and memory together, then
`decorateRelationships` and the diagnostics cross all four. So creating a card also
re-reads every document and every changelog fragment. There are 22 `invalidate()` calls in
`src/server/http.ts` and 17 in `src/modules/mcp/tools.ts`: 39 mutation points, one
all-or-nothing button.

Raising the TTL is not a free call: because the store is per-process, the TTL is also how a
running UI notices a card that an agent wrote through the MCP server or the CLI in a
*different* process. A longer TTL makes agent-driven changes appear later. That trade-off
belongs to the owner, which is why this is a card and not a patch.

Worth considering instead of, or alongside, a bigger TTL:

- Per-domain invalidation, so a card mutation does not discard the document index. Needs
  `buildProjectIndex` to be splittable, and the relationship decoration to be recomputed
  from cached domains rather than re-read.
- Cheap revalidation by `stat` instead of re-read: the walks now cost ~31 ms, so the
  remaining ~700 ms is reading and parsing 3 163 files. Comparing mtime and size could
  skip the parse when nothing changed.

Found while fixing the walk (see CHG-0012). Numbers above are post-fix.

Bumping the package version marks every generated agent file stale, even when
its content is byte-identical.

The generated blocks carry both a version stamp and a content digest:

    <!-- workfile:begin kind=canonical-agent-protocol version=0.7.0-rc.2
         digest=sha256:61354d4b... -->

Going from 0.7.0-rc.3 to 0.7.0-rc.4 flagged all six files (`AGENTS.md`,
`.project/agents/protocol.md` and the four workflows). Running `workfile agents sync`
changed the version stamp and nothing else — the digest was unchanged in all six.

So the check reads the version rather than the digest that is sitting next to it. Every
release therefore produces six warnings that mean nothing, which is the fastest way to
teach people to ignore `doctor` output.

Compare the digest. Keep the version stamp for information.

**Evidencia.** `src/server/http.ts:258` construye `new URL(request.url, "http://project.local")`, descartando la cabecera `Host`. No hay comprobación de `Origin`, `Referer` ni `Sec-Fetch-Site` en las 1.048 líneas del handler, y `readJson` (`http.ts:128-136`) hace `JSON.parse` sin mirar el `Content-Type`.

**Reproducido.**
- `curl -X POST .../api/v2/cards -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' --data '{"title":"CSRF probe","area":"api"}'` devolvió 201 y escribió la card en disco.
- `fetch(base + '/api/tasks', { headers: { Host: 'attacker.example.com' } })` devolvió 200 con todas las cards y el `repoRoot` absoluto.

`text/plain`, `x-www-form-urlencoded` y `multipart/form-data` son *simple requests*: el navegador las envía cross-origin sin preflight. Con DNS rebinding el atacante además está en el mismo origen y lee las respuestas.

**Propuesta.** Una función de guarda al principio del handler, antes del enrutado:
1. `Host` fuera de la allowlist (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]` + puerto de escucha) → 403.
2. `Origin` presente y distinto del host permitido → 403 `REQUEST_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN`.
3. `Sec-Fetch-Site` distinto de `same-origin`/`none` → 403.
4. Métodos mutadores sin `Content-Type: application/json` → 415 (así dejan de ser simple requests y el navegador obliga a preflight).

Un test por condición. Y que `workfile ui --host` distinto de loopback exija `--token` o `--allow-unauthenticated`.

La ruta de assets (`http.ts:293-311`) hace `sendBuffer` sin `X-Content-Type-Options`, sin `Content-Disposition`, sin CSP y sin `Cache-Control`. `sanitizeAssetName` (`http.ts:249-252`) permite cualquier extensión.

**Evidencia.** `cards.ts:59-81`, `docs.ts:190-204` y `changelog.ts:175-186` lanzan `Promise.all` sobre el conjunto completo de ficheros sin cota, y sus `catch` convierten **cualquier** excepción —EMFILE, ENFILE, ENOMEM, un fallo transitorio de E/S— en una entrada de `unreadable` con la misma forma que un fichero sin frontmatter. Ese resultado solo lo mira `doctor`; ningún listado ni la búsqueda lo consultan, así que la pérdida es silenciosa por diseño.

**Matiz importante** (corregido en verificación): Node ≥19 sube el soft limit al hard al arrancar, así que **no se reproduce** con el ulimit por defecto de Linux ni de macOS. Hace falta un **hard** limit ≲4096 — contenedores con `--ulimit nofile=N:N` o units de systemd con `LimitNOFILE=`. Es un defecto de robustez, no un fallo latente del núcleo.

**Propuesta.** `mapWithConcurrency(items, limit, fn)` en `src/core/concurrency.ts` (~30 líneas, cola con N workers, cero deps), límite `min(64, max(16, availableParallelism() * 8))`. Distinguir EMFILE/ENFILE en el catch y reintentar o abortar con `IO_DESCRIPTOR_EXHAUSTED` en vez de degradar a `unreadable`: un error de recurso del proceso no es un fichero ilegible.

tasks.body:
**Amplía T-0016, que sigue vigente en su totalidad.**

`createProjectIndexStore` (`records/index.ts:449-478`) tiene `maxAgeMs = 1000` y ningún caller lo sobreescribe. `loadedAt` se estampa **después** del build, así que la ventana útil es un segundo de reloj. Un turno de agente tarda más de 1 s ⇒ **ninguna** llamada MCP acierta la caché.

Y `invalidate()` lo tira todo: no hay granularidad por dominio, así que crear una card re-lee todos los documentos y todos los fragmentos. Hay 22 llamadas en `http.ts` y 17 en `mcp/tools.ts`: 39 puntos de mutación, un solo botón todo-o-nada.

**Por qué no basta con subir el TTL**: como el store es por proceso, el TTL es también el único modo en que una UI abierta se entera de lo que un agente escribió por MCP o CLI en **otro** proceso. Subirlo cambia velocidad por frescura. **Es el watcher lo que rompe el dilema** (ver el épico de reactividad).

**Propuesta.**
1. Guardar por fichero `{mtimeMs, size, revision}` y, en `get()`, hacer solo `stat`. Medido: `stat` de 2.967 ficheros = **50 ms** frente a 637 ms del build completo.
2. `invalidate(paths)` granular con `readRecordAt` por módulo, reparseando solo lo tocado.
3. Contador `epoch` monótono capturado antes del build, que descarta el resultado si cambió — arregla además una carrera real: hoy `invalidate()` no cancela la construcción en vuelo y se re-cachea el estado previo a la escritura.

**Riesgo a cubrir con test**: `readRecordAt` introduce un segundo camino de lectura junto al `load*` completo. Si divergen, el índice incremental sirve registros con forma distinta. Test obligatorio: build completo → tocar N ficheros → rebuild incremental → igualdad profunda contra un build completo posterior.

**Evidencia.** El servidor emite `ETag` en 14 sitios y **no lee `If-None-Match` en ninguno**. `sendJson` (`http.ts:83-90`) responde `Cache-Control: no-store` en todo JSON. No hay `zlib` en el fichero, así que `Accept-Encoding: gzip, br` se ignora.

**Medido**: `/api/tasks` = 3.811.159 bytes sin comprimir, re-descargados cada 30 s ⇒ ~457 MB/hora para, casi siempre, cero cambios.

**Propuesta.**
1. Helper `conditional()` con `If-None-Match` → 304, y `ETag` en **todas** las lecturas incluidas las listas (hash de las `revision` de la colección).
2. gzip con `node:zlib` por encima de ~1.400 bytes, con el buffer comprimido cacheado por `(ruta, params, epoch)`. Medido: 3,63 MiB → 162,9 KiB.
3. `Cache-Control` correcto: `no-cache` (revalidar) en JSON, `immutable` en los assets con hash de la UI.

*(Brotli descartado con medición: 14% mejor que gzip pero ~10× el coste de CPU en un servidor de un solo hilo.)*

Con 304 + proyección, el poll estacionario pasa de 3,8 MB a ~300 bytes.

tasks.body:
**Decisión clave, contra la intuición.** Tres auditorías propusieron `fs.watch(protocolRoot, {recursive: true})`. **Medido con Node 22 sobre un workspace real: la llamada bloquea el event loop 604-804 ms** (readdir recursivo síncrono). La colocación per-directory: **230 watchers en 4 ms**.

**Diseño.** Un `fs.watch` no recursivo por directorio, colocado con el mismo autómata de segmentos que ya usa `discoverFiles` (`glob.ts:86-150`). Alta de directorios nuevos con rescan, baja de borrados, umbral de overflow, tope `maxWatchedDirs` con degradación a polling.

**Filtros, antes de tocar nada** — todos verificados como necesarios:
- Ignorar `.cache/`: los locks de `withFileLock` (`locks.ts:20-41`) se crean y borran en **cada** mutación; sin este filtro el watcher se autoalimenta.
- Ignorar ficheros que empiecen por `.` y acaben en `.tmp`: los temporales de `writeFileAtomic` (`filesystem.ts:7`) se crean en el **mismo** directorio destino.
- Quedarse solo con `.md`.

**Debounce coalescente** de 120 ms con tope de 1.000 ms, acumulando rutas en un `Set`: un `agents sync` toca 6 ficheros y una release mueve N fragmentos.

**Supresión de eco**: **no** silenciar el watcher durante las escrituras propias — es una carrera irresoluble (medido: `writeFileAtomic` emite 5 eventos y el último llega 1-2 ms después del rename, pero bajo carga inotify puede tardar cientos). Comparar la `revision` sha256 recién escrita contra la que aparece en disco: inmune al tiempo.

**Autotest de arranque**: escribir y borrar `<cache>/.watch-probe` y esperar 500 ms; si no llega el evento, modo polling. `fs.watch` no dispara en sistemas de red, en `/mnt/*` de WSL2 ni en algunos bind mounts de Docker.

**El watcher solo acorta el camino**: un barrido de `stat` corre siempre que el último sea más viejo que `maxSweepAgeMs`. Un evento perdido degrada a 5 s de latencia, **nunca a incorrección**.

tasks.body:
**Evidencia.** `src/core/glob.ts:160-166`: la firma es `canDescendInto(directory, includePatterns)` — **solo includes**. Los `exclude` se aplican por entrada dentro de `discoverFiles` (`:191-197`), nunca en el autómata.

**Colisión entre tres diseños.** El watcher coloca con ese mismo autómata; el índice persistente escribe en `.project/.cache/index/`; la actividad de agentes escribe un JSONL por tool call en `.project/.cache/activity/`. Resultado: **bucle infinito** — hook escribe → watcher dispara → invalida índice → escribe índice → watcher dispara → SSE → la UI refetchea. Con Claude Code trabajando, `PostToolUse` se dispara decenas de veces por minuto.

**Propuesta.**
1. `canDescendInto(directory, includePatterns, excludePatterns)`, evaluando los excludes de directorio **dentro** del autómata; `discoverFiles` pasa a usarla.
2. Contrato escrito: `.project/.cache/` es **exclude duro, no configurable**. El watcher nunca lo mira. La invalidación del índice la dispara el escritor por llamada directa. La actividad de agentes llega a la UI por su propio canal.
3. Aviso en `doctor` cuando la superficie de watch supere unos cientos de directorios: es síntoma de un `docs.sources` mal acotado, no del watcher.

tasks.body:
**SSE, no WebSocket.** Razones concretas: el flujo es unidireccional (las mutaciones ya tienen rutas REST con `If-Match`), va sobre el `node:http` que ya existe sin dependencias (`ws` rompería el argumento de cero deps), `EventSource` reconecta solo con `Last-Event-ID`, y atraviesa cualquier proxy.

**Contrato.** `text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `flushHeaders()`. `Set<ServerResponse>` de suscriptores limpiado en `request.on('close')`. Heartbeat `:ping` cada 25 s con `.unref()`. Ring buffer de 512 para catch-up por `Last-Event-ID`, `serverId` para detectar reinicio, backpressure por `writableLength`.

**Eventos** con `id` = epoch del índice: `workspace.changed`, `record.changed` (`{id, kind, path, revision, op, fields}`), `record.deleted`, `health.changed`, `activity.changed`.

**Nunca mandar cuerpos por el canal**: el evento es una invalidación con metadatos; el cliente hace el GET si esa vista está montada.

**Un evento por ráfaga, no por registro**: un `git checkout` de 1.200 registros produciría 1.200 frames y 1.200 transacciones de store. Por encima de un umbral, emitir `sync.reset`.

Test: un `writeFile` externo produce `records.changed` en menos de 500 ms; un lote de 1.000 ficheros produce **exactamente un** `sync.reset`.

**Decisión: store propio, no TanStack Query.** El razonamiento no es el tamaño (~13 kB gzip, y todo el UI vive en devDependencies con `dist/ui` precompilado, así que no rompería nada). Es que **su modelo de frescura es `staleTime` + refetch, o sea polling** — exactamente lo que queremos eliminar. **Tres piezas, ~450 líneas:**
1. `store/records.ts`: `Map<id, Record>` normalizado + índices derivados por kind, expuesto con `useSyncExternalStore` y selectores memoizados por clave.
2. `store/query.ts`: deduplicación por clave, `AbortController`, `keepPreviousData` (elimina el parpadeo), estados `idle|loading|refreshing|error`.
3. `store/live.ts`: `EventSource` con reconexión y fallback a polling.

`react-remove-scroll` is a transitive dependency of `radix-ui`, which arrived
with the design system migration (T-0023).

## What it was not

- Not a phantom dependency: `react-remove-scroll` declares `tslib@^2.1.0`.
- Not the lockfile: `pnpm-lock.yaml` carries the `tslib: 2.8.1` edge, twelve times.
- Not the vite config, and not `--mode demo`.
- Not `NODE_ENV=production`.

A clean clone plus `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` plus `build:demo` always passes.

## Root cause

A `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` run **incrementally over an existing
`node_modules`** does not materialise `tslib@2.8.1`. It appears neither at
`node_modules/tslib`, nor beside its dependent in
`.pnpm/react-remove-scroll@.../node_modules/`, nor even as `.pnpm/tslib@2.8.1`.
It is the only package lost — diffing the `.pnpm` tree of a clean install
against an incremental one returns exactly one line.

Vercel restores `node_modules` from its build cache between deploys, so its
install is always the incremental case. The first deploy after swapping
`@primer/octicons-react` for `radix-ui` is precisely the transition that
triggers it.

Reproduced locally: install at `cea0ba9`, check out `main`, reinstall frozen —
the error comes back verbatim.

## What does not fix it

Declaring `tslib` in `devDependencies`. This was tried: the incremental install
still does not create `node_modules/tslib` and reports `Already up to date`.
The failure is in the installer, not the manifest, so the dependency was
reverted rather than left behind as noise.

## Fix

`--force` on the `installCommand` in `vercel.json`. It ignores the current
state of the tree and relinks everything. The install goes from ~1 s to ~41 s
with a warm store, which is a fair price for a build that compiles.

## Why this card exists after T-0023 and T-0098 were closed

Both were marked `done`. Neither was. Measured in a browser against this
workspace before any of the work below:

| view     | shadcn buttons / total | elements with `data-slot` |
|----------|------------------------|---------------------------|
| explorer | 2 / 30                 | 13 of 210                 |
| docs     | 2 / 83                 | 17 of 541                 |
| memory   | 1 / 15                 | 7 of 220                  |
| health   | 0 / 14                 | **0 of 109**              |

36 native `<button>` elements, 21 native `<select>` elements and 3,372 lines of
the hand-written design system were untouched. The primitives were imported
almost everywhere and painted almost nowhere.

The cause was not neglect, it was ADR-0005. Coexistence by layers puts the
framework inside `@layer` and the legacy system outside it, and unlayered CSS
wins the cascade unconditionally — so a view kept its exact appearance until
someone deleted its rules by hand. The decision was engineered to make the
interface not change, which is the opposite of what adopting a design system is
for. Closing the epic on "the scaffolding is in place" is what made a 7%
migration look finished.

## What this card did

- Deleted the legacy design system. `ui/src/styles.css`: 3,372 lines to 321 —
  registry tokens, the two domain colour axes, and the rendered-Markdown rules,
  which have no element to hang a class on.
- Switched the style to `radix-rhea` and regenerated every primitive.
- Added twelve components from the registry: table, card, dropdown-menu, tabs,
  tooltip, checkbox, scroll-area, popover, skeleton, alert, command,
  input-group.
- Rebuilt all nine views plus the shell, the drawer, the record tree, both
  editors, the presence strip and the new-card dialog on primitives and
  utilities.
- Removed the legacy `:root { font: 14px/1.5 }`. Every registry size token was
  12.5% smaller than upstream designed it: `h-8` resolved to 28px, not 32.

Result: explorer 25/34, triage 23/30, docs 50/84, memory 15/16, health 11/14.

## Defects found while doing it

- The Explorer table overflowed the viewport and cut the `Updated` column.
- The row status control was the only unstyled element on the page, while the
  priority control beside it was styled — the same row, two different systems.
- The sidebar collapse button rendered the inverted icon.
- Docs rendered `Edit` as bare text with no button affordance.
- The Memory tree badge came out as a deformed oval.

None of these produced a console error; all nine views reported zero.

## Deliberate deviations

- Row selects stay native, per CONV-0003: a Radix select portals its content,
  and in a virtualised table the row beneath can unmount while the popup is
  open. They are styled to match the trigger rather than left as browser
  chrome, which is what made one of them look broken.
- Two token tests — `radii come from the scale` and `typography comes from one
  token per family` — were deleted rather than rewritten against the registry
  scale. They were passing. That is a real coverage loss and it is recorded
  here rather than left to be discovered.

Supersedes the approach in [[ADR-0005]]; see [[ADR-0009]].

## Why this exists after T-0100 closed

T-0100 deleted the legacy design system and moved every view onto registry
primitives. That was necessary and it was not sufficient: the layouts were
still hand-built with raw Tailwind, which is not the same thing as using
shadcn. The user reviewed the result and rejected it — six screenshots, each
one a concrete defect rather than a matter of taste.

The cause was that nobody had read shadcn's own rules. They are published in
the project's repository under `skills/shadcn/rules/` and every complaint maps
onto one:

| reported | rule broken |
|---|---|
| controls of unequal height in one row | one `size` per row |
| cards with odd borders | `Card` / `CardHeader` / `CardTitle`, not a bordered div |
| text running the full 1440px | constrain the measure |
| buttons with no spacing or structure | flex/grid with `gap-*`, never `space-y-*` |
| icons out of proportion | `data-icon`, no size classes on the icon |
| colours in text and alerts | *"never raw colors for status indicators"* — use `Badge` variants or semantic tokens |

A seventh defect had nothing to do with styling: dragging a card across the
board gave no indication of which column would receive it.

## What changed

- All fourteen surfaces rebuilt on the real components, in parallel, each
  agent reading the primitive on disk before using it, with an adversarial pass
  behind it looking specifically for dropped `aria-*`, handlers and props.
- Twenty more registry components adopted, including the `Sidebar` primitive —
  trigger, rail and collapse behaviour — replacing a hand-rolled equivalent.
- `Field`/`FieldGroup` for every form, `Empty` for every empty state, `Item`
  for list rows, `ButtonGroup` for navigation clusters, `ToggleGroup` for the
  layout switch, `Kbd` for shortcut hints.
- Base colour `neutral` instead of `slate`: slate carries blue, so dark mode
  came out navy. Verified rather than eyeballed — background measures
  `lab(2.75 0 0)`, chroma zero.
- Geist bundled through `@fontsource-variable`, so the woff2 ships inside
  `dist/ui`. No CDN, no runtime dependency. The previous stack named no family
  that exists on Linux.
- Drop target now highlights on the hovered column, alongside the keyboard
  path's existing `aria-live` announcement.

## Measured, not asserted

The filter toolbar wrapped onto two lines and pushed `New card` below the
fold. Measuring rather than guessing: eleven controls needed 1,269px of a
1,184px row. `flex-wrap` breaks a row instead of shrinking a flexible child, so
removing it lets the search field absorb the difference. One row at 1280, 1440
and 1920, every control 32px.

Nine views screenshotted in both themes: zero console errors. 152 tests, doctor
clean, `dependencies` still exactly `@types/node` — the shadcn CLI placed
`cmdk`, `sonner`, `react-resizable-panels` and `next-themes` there and all four
were moved to devDependencies or removed.

## Correction worth keeping

In the dark Flow screenshot the muted text looked warm-tinted and was nearly
"fixed". Measuring first gave `lab(66.128 -0.00003 0.00001)` — neutral grey.
The cast was an artefact of the image, not the stylesheet. Measure before
changing a colour.

Follows [[T-0100]] and [[ADR-0009]].

## Why a third rebuild

T-0100 deleted the legacy design system; T-0101 rebuilt every surface against
shadcn's published composition rules. Both were technically correct and the
result was still rejected: the problem was never rule compliance, it was the
look itself. Iterating on the shadcn baseline kept making it worse.

The user designed the interface they actually want in Claude Design
(`Workfile Rediseño.zip`, `Workfile - Rediseño.dc.html`).
That file is the spec: tokens, layout, typography and every screen.

## What the spec defines

- IDE-like shell: 48px header (logo, version chip, breadcrumb, ⌘K search,
  doctor + SSE status chips, theme toggle, New card), 214px nav rail with
  per-view counts, fixed 376px inspector rail, 30px agent-ledger footer,
  command-palette overlay.
- Nine views: Explorer (facet rail + dense table), Triage, Flow, Epics,
  Timeline, Docs, Memory (collection lanes), History, Health.
- Bespoke oklch token set (light + dark via `data-theme`), Geist + Geist Mono,
  13px base, density compact/comfortable (34/42px rows).

## Approach

- Keep the data layer untouched: `api.ts`, `api.http.ts`, `api.demo.ts`,
  `types.ts`, `query.ts`, `store/live.ts`, `demo-data.json`.
- Rebuild the presentation from zero as plain CSS component classes ported
  1:1 from the design file. shadcn registry, Tailwind and the sidebar/drawer
  shell are removed; Radix primitives stay only where behaviour needs them.
- Every existing behaviour ports into the new skin: optimistic patch with
  revision, bulk edit, SSE-driven reload, URL state, demo mode, docs/memory/
  changelog editing, body and property editors, uploads, archive, keyboard
  triage, presence (as the ledger footer).
- UI copy stays English like the rest of the product; the Spanish strings in
  the mock are an artifact of the design conversation.

Supersedes the approach of [[T-0101]]. Decision recorded in [[ADR-0010]].

records.body: Auditoría end-to-end de `0.7.0-rc.4` (commit `cea0ba9`): siete lentes independientes sobre núcleo, servidor HTTP, frontend, design system, superficie de agentes, edición y producto; cuatro diseños arquitectónicos derivados de los hallazgos; y una pasada de refutación adversarial sobre los 22 hallazgos más arriesgados, más un crítico de completitud. Este documento es el **mapa**: la línea base medida, el orden de ejecución y el índice de registros. El detalle de cada hallazgo vive en su card. ## Línea base medida Medida sobre este repo y sobre un corpus de trabajo de 3.163 registros (~2.967 ficheros de protocolo, 8,2 MB), más un sintético de 8.201 registros para los extremos. | Métrica | Valor | |---|---| | `buildProjectIndex` | 637 ms (3.163 registros) · 1.377 ms (8.201) | | Arranque de Node + import del bundle | ~190-290 ms | | Fracción del tiempo de pared que es el índice | **~88%** | | `searchProjectRecords` por consulta | 269-658 ms | | `GET /api/tasks` | 3.811.159 B, sin gzip, sin ETag | | `GET /api/v2/agents/context` | 679 ms para devolver 257 B | | `project_search {limit: 5}` por MCP | 20.780 B (~5.200 tokens), payload duplicado | | `project_get_record` de un registro-hub | 57,8 KB (~14.800 tokens), 93% backlinks | | Bundle de la UI | 295.907 B / 86.524 B gzip, un solo chunk, cero `lazy` | | CSS | 2.924 líneas · ~25% reutilizable · ~57% por vista · ~8% muerto | | Cobertura de tests | 76/76, 83,78% global | ## Sobre el método De 138 hallazgos, 39 mencionan un corpus externo y **solo 1 se sostiene sin citar código de este repositorio**. El corpus grande se usó como banco de medición —con 18 cards no se descubre que una consulta cuesta 600 ms— pero los hallazgos son del código. Los 22 hallazgos críticos y altos pasaron por un verificador instruido a **refutar por defecto**. Los 22 sobrevivieron, pero con correcciones sustantivas que están incorporadas en las cards. Las que cambian una decisión: - EMFILE bajó de crítico a medio: Node ≥19 sube el soft limit al hard, hace falta un **hard** limit ≲4096. Ver [[LRN-0010]]. - El font stack roto en Linux bajó de crítico a medio: es cosmético. - `Knowledge.tsx` **no** está en el bundle JS (Rollup ni lo transforma); sí lo está su CSS. - El recuento de vistas reactivas estaba invertido: cinco con poll, cuatro sin nada. - Eliminar `metadata` del registro **no** es seguro, y `view=summary` por defecto rompería tres paneles de detalle. Ver [[LRN-0011]]. - `fs.watch` recursivo —propuesto por tres auditorías— bloquea el event loop. Ver [[LRN-0005]]. ## Orden de ejecución El crítico de completitud encontró seis colisiones entre los cuatro diseños. Dos determinan el orden y ninguna era evidente por separado: 1. **Ningún diseño agendaba la migración de la UI fuera de `/api/tasks`**, el endpoint legacy sin `q`, `limit` ni `offset` del que dependen los tres a la vez. Hacerla después del design system significa reescribir dos veces los mismos componentes. 2. **`canDescendInto` no conoce `exclude`**, así que el watcher vigilaría el mismo `.project/.cache` donde el índice persistente y la actividad de agentes escriben. Ver [[CONV-0002]]. Secuencia resultante: **Fase 0 — suelo.** Seguridad y correcciones. Casi todo esfuerzo S. Épicos: [[T-0020]] y [[T-0019]]. Incluye borrar la vertical Knowledge ([[T-0060]]) antes de tocar el CSS: rebajar antes de reconstruir. **Fase 1 — contrato de datos.** Banco de pruebas primero ([[T-0052]]) para congelar la línea base, después proyección y paginación. Épico [[T-0021]]. **Fase 2 — MCP que ahorra tokens.** Adelgazar el cable ([[T-0073]]) **antes** de añadir tools nuevas, o `tools/list` se dispara. Después [[T-0072]] y [[T-0074]]. **Fase 3 — UI a v2 y reactividad.** [[T-0057]] es el cuello de botella de todo lo demás. Épico [[T-0022]]. **Fase 4 — design system.** Con las capturas ya montadas ([[T-0069]]) y la guarda de dependencias en CI ([[T-0061]]). El `lazy` por vista ([[T-0065]]) va antes de reconstruir Explorer, Flow y Gantt: el orden no es negociable. Épico [[T-0023]]. **Fase 5 — agentes en vivo.** Épico [[T-0024]]. Prerrequisito duro: T-0018, porque pasar de 6 a ~22 ficheros generados sin arreglar el digest deja el doctor inservible. **Fase 6 — editor.** Épico [[T-0025]], con el codec de bloques ([[T-0031]]) y `patchCardBody` ([[T-0076]]) ya puestos. ## Los tres nudos Tres cosas que no se ven leyendo el código por partes: **Rendimiento y reactividad son el mismo trabajo.** El TTL de 1 s del índice es simultáneamente el cuello de botella y el único canal por el que una UI abierta se entera de lo que otro proceso escribió. Por eso no se puede subir, y por eso el watcher es lo que desbloquea ambos. Ver [[LRN-0006]] y [[T-0048]]. **El objetivo de editar desde la interfaz está bloqueado en el núcleo, no en el frontend.** `body` no está en `CARD_PATCHABLE_FIELDS`, así que ninguna superficie puede escribir el cuerpo de una card — y un agente que quiere anotar un resultado tiene que usar Write crudo, saltándose el lock, la revisión y la validación. Y `patchFrontmatter` corrompe el YAML de bloque, que es lo que escriben Obsidian, `yaml.dump` y cualquier LLM que emita YAML canónico. **La superficie MCP no permite ver el tablero.** Ninguna de las 22 tools es de listado y `project_search` exige query no vacía, así que la pregunta más frecuente de un agente —«¿qué hay en `doing`?»— no es expresable. Es el agujero más caro, porque empuja al agente a leer los ficheros a pelo, que es justo lo que el protocolo existe para evitar. ## Lo que ya está bien Merece quedar escrito, porque nada de lo anterior sugiere reescribir el núcleo: - `test/package-smoke.mjs` empaqueta con `npm pack`, instala el tarball en un consumidor limpio, **verifica que React no se instala en runtime**, typechequea los `.d.ts` publicados con `skipLibCheck: false` y arranca el servidor empaquetado. - `ui/src/api.ts` declara `ProjectApi = typeof httpApi` y la demo la implementa: TypeScript impide que diverjan. - `test/record-tree.test.mjs` falla si el runtime no puede stripear TS **y** `CI` está puesto: un skip que no puede volverse verde en silencio. - La poda del walk por autómata de segmentos (`src/core/glob.ts:86-150`) con el razonamiento escrito de por qué el prefijo literal no sirve, y test de equivalencia entre podar y no podar. - El read-only está enforced en la capa de mutación del core, no por superficie — salvo los tres huecos de [[T-0028]]. - El renderer Markdown no usa `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` y no emite ``: **no hay vector de XSS por contenido del repositorio**, y esa propiedad hay que conservarla en cualquier editor futuro. - `decorateRelationships` es lineal, no cuadrática. `inflight` deduplica builds concurrentes. El tokenizador hace NFD y elimina diacríticos. ## Decisiones abiertas Tres de las cuatro se implementaron y están `accepted`: [[ADR-0006]] reactividad, [[ADR-0007]] actividad de agentes y [[ADR-0008]] índice. Queda **una** abierta, y es la que más superficie mueve: [[ADR-0005]], migrar el design system a shadcn/ui con base radix. Sigue en `proposed` a propósito — es la única decisión del lote que introduce dependencias de terceros en la interfaz, y aunque viajen en `devDependencies` porque `dist/ui` se publica precompilado, el CLI de shadcn las escribe en `dependencies` por defecto y ahí se rompe el argumento central del paquete. ## Cierre de la auditoría Las 97 tarjetas del backlog derivado están cerradas salvo dos, y ninguna de las dos es código pendiente: - [[T-0014]] *0.7.0 estable* es una acción de publicación, no de desarrollo. - [[T-0023]] *design system* tiene sus doce hijas cerradas, pero su título dice migración a shadcn y **no existe un solo componente shadcn en el repo**. Lo entregado es el diagnóstico que lo motivaba —tokens en tres ejes, radios, elevación, transiciones, las ocho píldoras unificadas, overlays, virtualización, kanban accesible, Gantt, capturas, paleta y TreeView— más la fontanería de [[T-0061]]. Cerrarlo ahora sería dar por hecha una migración que no ha ocurrido. [[T-0015]] queda como idea sin comprometer. Dos desviaciones se habían implementado sin anotar y ya están registradas en sus tarjetas: [[T-0067]] usa drag and drop HTML5 nativo en lugar de `@dnd-kit` (la ruta de teclado y los anuncios `aria-live`, que era lo que la tarjeta pedía de verdad, sí están), y [[T-0065]] implementa Dialog, Sheet y Sidebar a mano en `Drawer.tsx` en lugar de sobre Radix.

records.title: CLI reference
records.body:
# CLI reference

Every command accepts the global options and returns stable machine-readable
errors with `--json`.

## Global options

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--root PATH` | Workspace root (default: discovered from the working directory) |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--expected-revision REV` | Reject the write when the file changed since it was read |
| `--dry-run` | Preview filesystem changes without applying them |
| `--force` | Replace conflicting generated files |
| `--read-only` | Disable MCP mutation tools |
| `--yes` | Accept initializer defaults without prompting |

Exit codes: `3` stale revision · `2` configuration error · `1` validation / not found.

## Workspace

```bash
project init [--root PATH] [--yes] [--dry-run] [--name NAME] [--language LANG]
project schema [--json]        # effective runtime schema (areas, vocabularies…)
project doctor [--json] [--severity error|warning] [--max-issues N] [--rebuild-cache]
project ui [--host HOST] [--port PORT]
project search QUERY [--kind card,doc,change,release,memory] [--limit N] [--json]
```

### Query grammar

One grammar, shared by the CLI, the HTTP API, MCP and the interface — the same
string returns the same answer everywhere, which it did not before.

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `billing retry` | free text over id, title, metadata and body, ranked |
| `"exact phrase"` | one term, not two |
| `status:doing` | field filter; narrows rather than ranking |
| `area:ui type:bug` | filters combine with AND |
| `-status:done` | negated filter |
| `-draft` | negated term |
| `tag:` / `claim:` | aliases for `tags` and `claimed_by` |

Field names are the record's own keys, so the vocabulary follows the runtime
schema rather than a second list. An unknown field matches nothing instead of
falling back to free text, which would quietly return everything.

Text is compared with diacritics folded, so `diseno` finds `Diseño`.

## Work (cards)

```bash
project card list [--status S] [--area A] [--type T] [--priority P] [--parent ID]
                  [--claimed-by ACTOR] [--unclaimed] [--tag TAG] [--updated-since DATE]
                  [--limit N] [--offset N] [--fields a,b] [--with-body] [--json]
project card show ID [--json]
project card create --title TITLE [--area AREA] [--type TYPE] [--priority PRIORITY]
project card patch ID --json-input FILE [--expected-revision REV]
project card claim ID --actor ACTOR [--scope PATH,PATH] [--force --reason TEXT]
project card release ID [--actor ACTOR] [--status next]
project card transition ID STATUS [--actor ACTOR]
project card archive ID
project card reopen ID [--status backlog]
project card reap [--dry-run] [--older-than HOURS] [--json]
```

Claims carry an actor and optional path scope; the server refuses overlapping
scopes and releases the claim when a card leaves `doing`.

Filter flags take comma-separated values (`--type bug,task`) and combine with
AND. `--json` omits the Markdown body and reports `bodyBytes` instead; ask for
it with `--with-body`, or pick exactly what you need with `--fields`. Responses
carry `total`, `offset` and `truncated`.

Options a command does not recognise are refused with `CLI_ARGUMENT_UNKNOWN`
rather than ignored, so a mistyped filter fails instead of quietly returning
everything.

A claim has a lifecycle, not just a flag. The card records `claimed_by` and
`claimed_at`; the live signal lives in `.project/.cache/activity/sessions/` and
therefore outside git, because a heartbeat written into frontmatter would leave
the working tree permanently dirty. `doctor` reports `card-claim-stale` past
`cards.claimLeaseHours` and `card-claim-orphaned` when a session stops
signalling, and `workfile card reap` releases them.

## Docs

```bash
project doc list [--query TEXT] [--managed] [--json]
project doc show ID [--json]
project doc create --title TITLE [--kind KIND] [--status STATUS] [--folder PATH]
project doc move ID --folder PATH [--expected-revision REV]
project doc patch ID --json-input FILE [--expected-revision REV]
```

Indexed documents (from configured globs) get deterministic `PATH-*` IDs and are
read-only; managed documents live in `.project/docs/` with `DOC-NNNN` IDs.

Managed documents are loaded recursively, so folders work even when they are
created by hand. `docs.layout` decides where new documents are written — `kind`
(the default) groups them into a folder named after the document kind, `flat`
uses the managed root — and `--folder PATH` overrides it for a single command.
The path must stay inside `docs.managedPath`; `--folder ""` targets the root.
`workfile doc move` relocates a document without changing its ID or its content.

## History (changelog)

```bash
project changelog list [--unreleased] [--visibility public|internal] [--json]
project changelog show ID [--json]
project changelog add --title TITLE [--type fixed] [--area AREA]
project changelog patch ID --json-input FILE [--expected-revision REV]
project changelog preview [--fragments CHG-0001,CHG-0002]
project changelog release VERSION [--fragments CHG-0001,CHG-0002] [--title TITLE]
project changelog render [--visibility public|internal] [--write]
project changelog verify
```

Release version validation follows `changelog.releaseStrategy`: `semver`,
`calendar` or `freeform`.

## Memory

```bash
project memory list [--collection learnings] [--status active] [--json]
project memory show ID [--json]
project memory add COLLECTION --title TITLE [--status STATUS]
project memory patch ID --json-input FILE [--expected-revision REV]
project memory graduate ID --to CONV-0001,DOC-0001
project memory supersede ID --by ID
project memory verify
```

`add` accepts singular aliases (`learning`, `decision`, `incident`, `convention`,
`context`) as well as collection ids. Collections and prefixes:

| Collection | Prefix | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| learnings | `LRN` | Reusable observations with confidence and occurrences |
| decisions | `ADR` | Proposed / accepted / rejected / superseded decisions |
| incidents | `INC` | Operational events with severity and resolution metadata |
| conventions | `CONV` | Durable rules for humans and agents |
| context | `CTX` | Useful but potentially expiring project state |

## Agents

```bash
project agents sync [--targets agents-md,claude,cursor,copilot]
project agents check [--targets ...]
project agents context --card T-0001 [--limit 20]
```

`sync` writes compact managed blocks (version + SHA-256 digest) into `AGENTS.md`,
`CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md` without touching
unrelated content. `context` returns a bounded, prioritized context bundle for a card.

## CI templates

```bash
project ci sync [--targets github,gitlab,generic]
project ci check [--targets ...]
```

## Legacy migration

```bash
project migrate plan [--source .planning] [--mode copy|move]
project migrate apply [--source .planning] [--mode copy|move] [--force]
project migrate schema [--dry-run] [--json]
```

Valid v1 cards become canonical v2 records; everything else is preserved under
`.project/sources/legacy-planning/` with a written migration report.

`migrate schema` is a different job: it moves a workspace forward when the
installed package expects a newer `schemaVersion` than `.project/VERSION`
declares. Steps run in ascending order under a lock, `--dry-run` prints the plan
without writing, and the result is recorded in `.project/migrations/schema.json`
along with `upgradedWith` in `.project/VERSION`. A workspace *newer* than the
package is refused with `WORKSPACE_SCHEMA_AHEAD` — upgrade the package instead.

## MCP

```bash
project mcp [serve] [--read-only]
project mcp inspect [--json]
project mcp config [--read-only] [--json]
```

See [mcp.md](mcp.md) for the server contract.

# Getting started

Workfile coordinates **Work, Docs, History and durable Memory** as markdown
files inside your repository. This guide takes you from zero to a working workspace.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @illodev/workfile     # per repository (recommended)
pnpm workfile doctor              # dependency bins run through pnpm / npx

pnpm add -g @illodev/workfile     # or globally: `project` lands on your PATH
```

`pnpm dlx @illodev/workfile init` works for one-shot initialization, but keep the
package installed afterwards — that is what makes the `project` commands resolve.

## Initialize a workspace

```bash
project init
```

The initializer detects your package manager, monorepo folders, likely card areas,
documentation sources, agent environments and CI providers. Every answer can be
given as a flag for automation, and `--dry-run` prints the exact filesystem plan:

```bash
project init --yes --language es --agents agents-md,claude --ci github
project init --dry-run --json
```

You get a `project.config.mjs` at the root and a `.project/` directory:

```text
project.config.mjs
.project/
├── VERSION
├── cards/            # Work records (T-NNNN), archive/ for closed history
├── assets/           # files attached to cards
├── docs/             # managed documents (DOC-NNNN)
├── changelog/        # unreleased/ fragments and releases/
├── memory/           # learnings, decisions, incidents, conventions, context
└── agents/           # canonical agent instructions
```

All of it is plain markdown with frontmatter — commit everything except
`.project/.cache/` (the initializer adds it to `.gitignore` for you).

## The daily loop

```bash
project ui                       # local board at http://127.0.0.1:4747
project card create --title "Ship the login page" --area web
project card claim T-0001 --actor agent-a1 --scope apps/web
project card transition T-0001 review --actor agent-a1
```

Agents claim cards with scoped paths so two of them never touch the same files;
claims release automatically when a card leaves `doing`.

As work lands, record it:

```bash
project changelog add --title "Login page" --type added --area web
project memory add learning --title "Session cookies need SameSite=Lax"
project doc create --title "Auth runbook" --kind runbook
```

And when you cut a version, the accumulated fragments become a release:

```bash
project changelog preview
project changelog release 1.4.0
project changelog render --visibility public --write   # regenerates CHANGELOG.md
```

## Keeping it healthy

```bash
project doctor --json
```

The doctor validates every collection: broken references, stale docs, expired
context, incidents missing resolution metadata, unmanaged agent instructions.
The same diagnostics power the Health view in the UI.

## Where to go next

- [CLI reference](cli.md) — every command and flag.
- [HTTP API](http-api.md) — the same operations over REST.
- [MCP server](mcp.md) — expose the workspace to AI agents.
- [SPEC](SPEC.md) — the normative protocol specification.

# HTTP API

`workfile ui` starts the local server (default `http://127.0.0.1:4747`). The same
core services back the CLI, the MCP server and the UI — the API is a thin layer.

## Conventions

- Managed record reads expose an `ETag`; mutations accept `If-Match` and reject
  stale writes with a conflict error.
- Errors use stable codes:

```json
{
    "error": {
        "code": "MEMORY_WRITE_CONFLICT",
        "message": "The memory record changed after it was loaded.",
        "details": {}
    }
}
```

- List endpoints accept `q`, `limit` and `offset`; responses carry `total`.
- List endpoints also accept `view=full|summary|list` and `fields=a,b,c`.
  `summary` replaces the Markdown body with `bodyBytes` and a 200-character
  `excerpt` and reduces the link arrays to ids and relations; `list` drops the
  excerpt too. `fields` overrides the view and returns exactly those keys.
  Measured on 100 records: 169 KB full, 70 KB summary, 43 KB list, 6.7 KB for
  three fields.
  `full` is the default deliberately — the packaged UI still renders record
  bodies out of its list responses — so narrowing is opt-in until it fetches
  what it displays.
- Collection reads carry an `ETag` over the page they return, and honour
  `If-None-Match` with a `304`. Cards are the corpus a polling client re-fetches
  most, so this is where it matters: the steady state costs a header exchange.
- JSON responses above ~1.4 KB are gzipped when `Accept-Encoding` allows it,
  with `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. Brotli is not offered: ~14% smaller for roughly
  an order of magnitude more CPU on a single-threaded server.
- `Cache-Control` is `no-cache` — revalidate every time, but a revalidation may
  answer `304`. It is deliberately not `no-store`, which would forbid that.

## Events

`GET /api/v2/events` is a Server-Sent Events stream of workspace changes.

```
event: hello
data: {"serverId":"aec9c77abfc871ec","lastEventId":0}

id: 1
event: records.changed
data: {"epoch":1,"count":1,"paths":[".project/cards/T-0042-example.md"]}
```

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `hello` | Sent on connect. `serverId` distinguishes a reconnection to the same process from one to a restarted process whose ids began again. |
| `records.changed` | Files changed. Carries the paths and the new index `epoch`. |
| `activity.changed` | A card write may have changed who is working on what. A separate event so a presence view need not refetch records. |
| `sync.reset` | Too many paths at once (a `git checkout`, a release), or the client's `Last-Event-ID` fell off the ring buffer. Refetch rather than applying a delta. |

Events are **invalidations, not payloads**: no record body ever travels down the
channel. The client fetches what the view it has mounted actually needs.

The source is a file watcher over the protocol corpus, so it sees every writer —
the CLI, an agent over MCP, git, an editor — not only mutations made through
this server. `.project/.cache` is excluded: it holds the locks that churn on
every write, the persisted index and agent activity, so watching it would feed
back into itself.

`EventSource` reconnects on its own and resumes with `Last-Event-ID`. The
watcher is a fast path and not the source of truth — `fs.watch` is silent on
network filesystems and its queue is bounded — so the index still revalidates
against the filesystem. A dropped event costs latency, never correctness.

## Diagnostics

`GET /api/v2/metrics` reports request counts per route, p50/p95 latency over the
last thousand requests, the index epoch, connected event clients and the
watcher's mode. `workfile ui --verbose` (or `PROJECT_LOG=1`) also writes one line
per request to stderr, and any 5xx logs its stack — which nothing did before, so
an error shown in the interface had no counterpart anywhere to diagnose it from.

## Activity

`GET /api/v2/activity` answers who is working on what, combining three signals
that already existed and that nothing joined up:

- the lock files `withFileLock` writes, which exist exactly as long as a write
  does — the most precise "right now" the system has;
- the durable claims in card frontmatter (`claimed_by`, `claimed_at`, `scope`);
- session heartbeats under `.project/.cache/activity/sessions/`.

Each claim carries a derived `state`: `live` (a session is signalling),
`held`, `stale` (past `cards.claimLeaseHours`) or `orphaned` (a session that
stopped signalling). That distinction is the point — a claim from four minutes
ago and one from a process that died three days ago looked identical before.

`conflicts` lists claims by *different* actors whose scopes overlap. This is the
situation claims exist to prevent, and it was computed inside `claimCard` and
then thrown away with the response.

## Request guard

The server holds unauthenticated read and write access to the repository, so the
browser's own origin rules are the entire security model. Every request is
checked before routing:

| Condition | Response |
| --- | --- |
| `Host` outside the allowlist, or its port is not the listening port | `403 REQUEST_HOST_FORBIDDEN` |
| `Sec-Fetch-Site` present and not `same-origin` / `none` | `403 REQUEST_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN` |
| `Origin` present and outside the allowlist | `403 REQUEST_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN` |
| `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` with a CORS-simple or missing `Content-Type` | `415 REQUEST_CONTENT_TYPE_INVALID` |

The allowlist is `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `::1`, plus the bind address when
`--host` names a specific non-wildcard interface.

The last rule matters as much as the others: `text/plain`,
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data` and *no* content type
at all are CORS-simple, so a cross-origin page could send them without a
preflight. Requiring anything else forces a preflight, which this server never
answers.

Practical consequence for clients: **mutations must set an explicit
`Content-Type`**. Use `application/json` for the JSON API and
`application/octet-stream` (or any concrete binary type) for asset uploads. A
`fetch` that passes a `File` or an `ArrayBuffer` without setting the header will
be refused.

Non-browser clients are unaffected — `curl` sends no `Origin` and no
`Sec-Fetch-Site`, and its `Host` is the loopback address it dialled.

Assets are served with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a
`default-src 'none'; sandbox` CSP, and `Content-Disposition: attachment` for
anything outside a narrow inline allowlist. Uploads of types that can execute
script (`.html`, `.svg`, `.mjs`, …) are refused with
`400 ASSET_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`.

## Workspace and index

```text
GET  /api/v2/workspace
GET  /api/v2/schema
GET  /api/v2/health
GET  /api/v2/records?q=&kind=&limit=&offset=
GET  /api/v2/search?q=&kind=&limit=&offset=
GET  /api/v2/records/:id
```

## Work

```text
GET/POST  /api/v2/cards
PATCH     /api/v2/cards/:id
POST      /api/v2/cards/:id/claim
POST      /api/v2/cards/:id/transition
POST      /api/v2/cards/:id/archive
POST      /api/v2/cards/:id/reopen
POST      /api/v2/cards/bulk
```

## Docs

```text
GET/POST   /api/v2/docs
GET/PATCH  /api/v2/docs/:id
```

## History

```text
GET/POST   /api/v2/changelog
GET/PATCH  /api/v2/changelog/:id
POST       /api/v2/changelog/releases/preview
POST       /api/v2/changelog/releases
GET/POST   /api/v2/changelog/render
```

## Memory

```text
GET/POST   /api/v2/memory
GET/PATCH  /api/v2/memory/:id
POST       /api/v2/memory/:id/graduate
POST       /api/v2/memory/:id/supersede
```

## Agents and CI

```text
GET   /api/v2/agents
POST  /api/v2/agents/sync
GET   /api/v2/agents/context?card=T-0001
GET   /api/v2/ci
POST  /api/v2/ci/sync
```

## MCP inspection

```text
GET  /api/v2/mcp
GET  /api/v2/mcp/config
```

## Legacy routes

`/api/tasks`, `/api/health` and `/api/knowledge` remain for existing callers.
The packaged UI no longer uses the first two: it boots from
`/api/v2/workspace` (identity plus the runtime schema) and reads
`/api/v2/cards`, which — unlike `/api/tasks` — honours `q`, `limit`, `offset`
and `view`, and carries an ETag.

Asset upload is still `POST /api/tasks/:id/assets`; it has no v2 equivalent yet.

New integrations should target `/api/v2/*`.

records.body:
# MCP server

Workfile includes a local, dependency-free MCP server speaking UTF-8,
newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio. Every operation delegates to the same core
services used by the CLI and HTTP API.

```bash
project mcp                    # serve over stdio
workfile-mcp --root /path/to/repository
project mcp --read-only        # mutation tools removed from tools/list
project mcp inspect --json     # tool/resource/prompt inventory
project mcp config --json      # portable client process configuration
```

## Reading the workspace

`project_card_list`, `project_doc_list`, `project_changelog_list` and
`project_memory_list` answer "what is in here" without needing a search query.
They take filters (`status`, `area`, `type`, `priority`, `parent`, `claimedBy`,
`unclaimed`, `tags`, `updatedSince`) and return a compact row per record — no
Markdown body, no `revision`.

`project_next` answers the question an agent actually has: which cards can be
started now. It excludes epics and anything with unmet dependencies, puts work
already claimed by the caller first, and attaches the reason each candidate
qualified.

Listings deliberately omit `revision`. Writing needs a read-then-write —
`project_get_record` returns the current revision, which `expectedRevision`
then guards — and carrying a possibly-stale one in a list only invites a
conflict.

Every result carries the data once, in `structuredContent`; `content` is a
one-line summary rather than a second copy of the payload. When a result would
exceed `maxToolResultBytes` it is truncated with a `truncated` marker instead of
failing the call, because a get-by-id has no query to narrow.

## Claude Code integration

```bash
project claude install     # generate the surface into the repository
project claude check       # report drift, exit 1 when anything is stale
```

`install` writes, as managed blocks that a resync updates without touching
anything around them:

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `.mcp.json` | Registers `workfile-mcp` — the binary that parses its own flags |
| `.claude/commands/{next,claim,done,context}.md` | Slash commands over one CLI call each |
| `.claude/skills/workfile/SKILL.md` | Projects `.project/agents/protocol.md` rather than restating it |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Three hooks |

**`SessionStart`** injects the board once — cards in flight, who holds them,
which paths they cover — so a session begins informed without reading a record.
Once per session, not per prompt: per-prompt injection accumulates in the
window.

**`PreToolUse`** on `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit` compares the target path against
the scope of cards claimed by *other* actors and answers `ask` with the card and
the actor named. It also asks when something writes a `.project/` record
directly, because that skips the lock, the revision check and validation.

It asks; it never denies. A guard rail that blocks too much gets switched off,
and then it protects nothing.

**`PostToolUse`** appends one line to `.project/.cache/activity/events.jsonl`,
asynchronously.

The hook runtime (`dist/src/runtime/claude/hooks.mjs`) imports nothing from this
package. `src/index.js` re-exports thirteen modules and several read
`package.json` at load, and `PreToolUse` runs before *every* tool call in the
session — not only the ones it might block. A test pins its p95.

Generated files grant permissions in someone else's repository, so
`allowed-tools` names the exact subcommand (`Bash(workfile card claim *)`), never
`Bash(project *)`. `.claude/settings.json` and `.mcp.json` are merged, not
replaced: a ledger in `.project/generated/claude-code.json` records which keys
are generated so removing one later actually removes it.

### Installing as a plugin

The same surface is distributed as a Claude Code plugin, for repositories that
would rather not have generated files committed:

```
/plugin marketplace add illodev/workfile
/plugin install workfile@illodev
```

The plugin registers the MCP server with `--root ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` and
resolves its hooks through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, so it works without the
package being a dependency of the repository at all.

Both forms exist on purpose. A plugin's `settings.json` accepts only `agent` and
`subagentStatusLine`, so anything else has to be generated locally; and a
generator alone means every version bump leaves the written files behind, which
is the trap `T-0018` recorded. `scripts/build-plugin.mjs` assembles the plugin
from the same functions `project claude install` uses, and a test asserts the
packaged runtime is byte-identical to the source — a hook that behaves
differently depending on how it was installed is a bug nobody would find.

## Protocol revisions

The server is dual-era:

- **Modern `2026-07-28`** — stateless per-request `_meta`, `server/discover`,
  `resultType` and cache metadata.
- **Legacy `2025-11-25`** and earlier declared revisions — the
  `initialize` / `notifications/initialized` lifecycle for existing hosts.

## Tools (22)

Read-only:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `project_workspace` | Workspace, config and module overview |
| `project_search` | Unified weighted search across all collections |
| `project_get_record` | Any record by stable ID |
| `project_doctor` | Full health diagnostics |
| `project_agent_context` | Bounded, prioritized context for a card |

Mutations (absent in `--read-only` mode; rejected with `MCP_SERVER_READ_ONLY`):

| Domain | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Work | `project_card_create`, `project_card_patch`, `project_card_claim`, `project_card_transition`, `project_card_archive`, `project_card_reopen` |
| Docs | `project_doc_create`, `project_doc_move`, `project_doc_patch` |
| History | `project_changelog_add`, `project_changelog_patch`, `project_changelog_preview`, `project_changelog_release` |
| Memory | `project_memory_add`, `project_memory_patch`, `project_memory_graduate`, `project_memory_supersede` |

Tool descriptions carry read-only, destructive and idempotency annotations.

## Resources and prompts

- **Resources:** `project://workspace`, `project://health`, `project://protocol`,
  `project://record/{id}`.
- **Prompts:** `start-work`, `finish-work`, `record-knowledge`.

## Process hygiene

stdout is reserved exclusively for MCP messages; diagnostics go to stderr.
`workfile mcp config` emits the Node executable, the **`workfile-mcp` binary**,
workspace root, preferred protocol revision and optional `--read-only` flag, so
hosts can build their own client configuration — client-specific files stay
outside the canonical repository protocol.

It names the dedicated binary rather than `workfile mcp` on purpose: the
multiplexed CLI takes the third argument as a subcommand, so a `--root` in that
position is not a flag it can parse. `test/mcp.test.mjs` spawns exactly what the
helper returns and drives a handshake through it, so the emitted command cannot
drift into being unrunnable again.

records.body:
# Workfile

`@illodev/workfile` is a repository-native protocol for coordinating **Work, Docs,
History and durable project Memory** between humans and software agents.

Markdown files in the repository are canonical. The CLI, HTTP API and local UI use the
same core services, collection registry, index and validation rules. No exclusive state
is kept in the browser or in a database.

> Current implementation: **0.7.0-rc.2 — TypeScript Release Candidate**. Work, Docs,
> History and Memory share the common `ProjectRecord` index. The core, CLI, HTTP server and
> MCP runtime are authored in TypeScript and distributed as compiled ESM with public
> declarations. The local UI is precompiled and included in the package.

**[Try the live demo](https://workfile-ochre.vercel.app)** — it replays this
repository's own workspace: the real cards, releases, incidents and learnings of
Workfile's development. Mutations work per browser session and reset on reload.

![The Flow board: execution columns with an agent claim active on the card being worked on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illodev/workfile/main/.github/media/flow.png)

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or newer.
- npm, pnpm, yarn or Bun may invoke the package.

## Install

Every `project …` command in this README requires the package to be installed —
`pnpm dlx` / `npx` one-offs run a command and discard the binary afterwards:

```bash
pnpm add -D @illodev/workfile     # per repository (recommended)
pnpm workfile doctor              # dependency bins run through pnpm / npx

pnpm add -g @illodev/workfile     # or globally: `project` lands on your PATH
project doctor
```

`pnpm dlx @illodev/workfile init` is fine for one-shot initialization, but keep the
package as a devDependency afterwards: that is what makes the `project` scripts that
`init` adds to package.json resolve.

## TypeScript API

The published surface exposes JavaScript and declarations through conditional package
exports. TypeScript consumers receive typed configuration, workspace, record, search and
integration contracts from the root package and every documented subpath:

```ts
import {
    defineProject,
    type CardStatus,
    type ProjectConfig,
    type ProjectRecord
} from "@illodev/workfile";
import { createSemanticSearchProvider } from "@illodev/workfile/search";

const config: ProjectConfig = defineProject({
    schemaVersion: 2,
    name: "Billing",
    cards: {
        areas: ["api", "web"]
    }
});

const status: CardStatus = "doing";
```

The CLI and UI do not require TypeScript in consuming projects. React, Primer, Vite and the
UI type packages are build-only dependencies; the installed package serves bundled browser
assets from `dist/ui`.

## Workspace

A project is discovered through `project.config.mjs` and normally stores protocol-owned
files under `.project/`:

```text
project.config.mjs
.project/
├── VERSION
├── cards/
│   └── archive/
├── assets/
├── docs/
├── changelog/
│   ├── unreleased/
│   └── releases/
├── memory/
│   ├── learnings/
│   ├── decisions/
│   ├── incidents/
│   ├── conventions/
│   └── context/
├── agents/
└── .cache/
```

Minimal configuration:

```js
import { defineProject } from "@illodev/workfile";

export default defineProject({
    schemaVersion: 2,
    name: "My project",
    language: "es",
    cards: {
        areas: ["api", "web", "infra", "docs"]
    },
    docs: {
        sources: [
            "README.md",
            "docs/**/*.md",
            "apps/*/README.md",
            ".project/specs/**/*.md"
        ]
    },
    changelog: {
        releaseStrategy: "semver",
        defaultVisibility: "public"
    },
    memory: {
        collections: [
            "learnings",
            "decisions",
            "incidents",
            "conventions",
            "context"
        ]
    },
    agents: {
        targets: ["agents-md", "cursor"]
    },
    ci: {
        targets: ["github"]
    },
    mcp: {
        allowMutations: true
    },
    search: {
        semanticWeight: 0.35,
        maxProviderRecords: 500
    }
});
```

Project-specific areas, paths and vocabularies are resolved at runtime and exposed through
the effective schema. The eight Work statuses and the schema-v2 memory collection
semantics remain protocol contracts.

## Work

Cards are managed Markdown records under `.project/cards/`. The Work module provides
hierarchy, dependencies, claims, scope, status transitions, archives, assets and
conflict-aware writes.

```bash
project card list --json
project card show T-0042 --json
project card create --title "Implement runtime schema" --area infra
project card claim T-0042 --actor agent-56a30d1b --scope apps/api,packages/sdk
project card transition T-0042 review --actor agent-56a30d1b
project card patch T-0042 --json-input changes.json --expected-revision sha256:...
project card archive T-0042
project card reopen T-0042 --status backlog
```

## Docs

Docs combines two sources without copying existing documentation:

- **Indexed documents** discovered from configured globs. They receive deterministic
  `PATH-*` IDs and remain read-only through the protocol.
- **Managed documents** stored in `.project/docs/` with stable `DOC-NNNN` IDs, typed
  frontmatter and revision-aware mutations.

Managed documents are read recursively, so they can be grouped in folders — including
folders you create by hand. IDs stay global and sequential: a folder is organization,
not identity. New documents follow `docs.layout` (`kind`, the default, groups them by
document kind; `flat` writes them to the managed root) and `--folder` overrides it.

```bash
project doc list --query billing
project doc show DOC-0012 --json
project doc create --title "Deployment runbook" --kind runbook --status current
project doc create --title "Rate limiting" --folder architecture/billing
project doc move DOC-0012 --folder architecture
project doc patch DOC-0012 --json-input changes.json --expected-revision sha256:...
```

The doctor detects broken local links, unresolved related or superseded records, missing
scope paths and stale review/source relationships.

## History

History uses atomic change fragments rather than asking multiple branches or agents to
edit one shared `CHANGELOG.md`.

Unreleased fragment:

```yaml
---
id: CHG-0042
title: Add portable history workspace
type: added
area: infra
visibility: public
cards: [T-0042]
created: 2026-07-28
updated: 2026-07-28
---
```

A release consumes selected fragments, moves them beneath the release directory and
creates a canonical `REL-NNNN` record. Public or internal changelogs are derived output.

```bash
project changelog list --unreleased
project changelog add --title "Add portable history" --type added --area infra
project changelog preview
project changelog release 0.4.0 --title "History and Memory"
project changelog render --visibility public
project changelog render --visibility public --write
project changelog verify
```

Release versions can use `semver`, `calendar` or `freeform` validation according to
configuration. Fragments and releases participate in the same workfile search and backlink
graph as cards, docs and memory.

## Memory

Memory is a set of typed, atomic and lifecycle-aware records rather than a single growing
conversation transcript:

| Collection | Prefix | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Learnings | `LRN` | Reusable observations with confidence and occurrence signals |
| Decisions | `ADR` | Proposed, accepted, rejected or superseded decisions |
| Incidents | `INC` | Operational events, severity, timing and corrective actions |
| Conventions | `CONV` | Durable rules followed by humans and agents |
| Context | `CTX` | Useful but potentially expiring project state |

```bash
project memory list --collection learnings --status active
project memory add learning --title "Atomic fragments avoid merge conflicts" \
  --confidence high
project memory add decision --title "Keep Markdown canonical" --status accepted
project memory add incident --title "Release pipeline stalled" --severity high
project memory graduate LRN-0004 --to CONV-0002,DOC-0012
project memory supersede ADR-0003 --by ADR-0009
project memory patch CTX-0002 --json-input changes.json --expected-revision sha256:...
project memory verify
```

The doctor checks invalid lifecycle states, missing graduation/supersession targets,
expired context and incomplete incident resolution metadata.

## Unified index

Every module normalizes its files as `ProjectRecord` entries through a common collection
registry. The derived process-local index provides:

- weighted full-project text search;
- lookup by stable record ID;
- outgoing references and incoming backlinks across all four domains;
- card `source:` links and local Markdown links;
- module-specific health, lifecycle and freshness signals;
- module and collection counts.

Canonical state always remains on disk. The server cache is short-lived, invalidatable and
fully rebuildable.

```bash
project search "billing architecture"
project search release --kind change,release,memory --limit 25 --json
```

## Initialization

The initializer can run interactively or deterministically in automation. It detects the
package manager, monorepo folders, likely card areas, documentation sources, existing agent
environments and CI providers. A dry run exposes the exact filesystem plan.

```bash
pnpm dlx @illodev/workfile init
pnpm dlx @illodev/workfile init --yes --language es \
  --agents agents-md,claude,cursor,copilot --ci github
project init --dry-run --json
```

The generated `project.config.mjs` exports a plain object, so a workspace initialized via
`pnpm dlx` remains loadable before the package is installed locally. Existing files are not
overwritten unless `--force` is explicit. `.project/.cache/` is added to `.gitignore`; all
canonical protocol files remain tracked.

## Hosted demo

The UI ships with a demo mode for static hosting (Vercel, GitHub Pages, any file server).
`npm run build:demo` builds the UI with an in-memory API that replays a snapshot of a seeded
workspace: every view works and mutations behave normally for the session, then reset on
reload. The repository includes a `vercel.json`, so importing it into Vercel deploys the
demo with zero configuration.

```bash
pnpm run demo:data   # reseed and resnapshot ui/src/demo-data.json (needs build:core)
pnpm run build:demo  # static demo build into dist/ui
```

Regular builds tree-shake the demo layer and snapshot out of the bundle.

## Releasing

Releases publish from CI via npm [trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers)
(OIDC) — no npm token is stored in the repository. The circuit:

1. Cut the changelog: `workfile changelog release <version>` and `workfile changelog render --write`.
2. Bump and tag: `npm version <version>` then `git push && git push --tags`.
3. The `Release` workflow verifies the tag matches `package.json`, runs
   `check:release` (build, typechecks, tests, audit and a packaged-tarball smoke)
   with pnpm, and publishes with the npm CLI — prereleases (`x.y.z-*`) under the
   `next` dist-tag, stable versions under `latest`.

One-time setup: the very first publish must be manual
(`npm publish --provenance=false --tag next`, after removing `"private": true`),
because npm's trusted publisher can only be configured on an existing package.
After that, register this repository and `release.yml` as the package's trusted
publisher on npmjs.com.

## Agent Protocol

Canonical instructions and workflows live under `.project/agents/`. Compact managed blocks
are synchronized into supported environments without replacing unrelated user content:

```text
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
.cursor/rules/workfile.mdc
.github/copilot-instructions.md
```

```bash
project agents sync
project agents sync --targets agents-md,claude,cursor,copilot
project agents check
project agents context --card T-0042
```

Managed blocks carry the package version and a SHA-256 digest. `agents check` and
`workfile doctor` report missing, unmanaged or stale generated instructions. Agent context is
bounded and prioritizes the selected card, direct relationships, active conventions,
unresolved incidents and non-expired context instead of loading all workfile memory.

## Model Context Protocol

Workfile includes a local, dependency-free MCP server using UTF-8,
newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio. It delegates every operation to the same core
services used by the CLI and HTTP API, speaks both the modern (`2026-07-28`) and legacy
(`2025-11-25`) protocol revisions, and exposes 22 tools, four resources and three
prompts. Mutation tools disappear entirely in `--read-only` mode.

```bash
project mcp
project mcp inspect --json
project mcp config --read-only --json
```

The full contract — tool inventory, resources, prompts and process hygiene — is
documented in [`docs/mcp.md`](docs/mcp.md).

## Search integrations

Lexical search remains deterministic and local. Hosts may inject an optional semantic
provider programmatically; Workfile never selects a vendor or sends repository
content over the network by itself.

```js
import {
    createSemanticSearchProvider,
    searchProjectRecordsHybrid
} from "@illodev/workfile/search";

const provider = createSemanticSearchProvider({
    id: "company-embeddings",
    async search({ query, records }) {
        // Return [{ id, score }] with scores between 0 and 1.
        return rankWithYourApprovedProvider(query, records);
    }
});

const result = await searchProjectRecordsHybrid(index.records, query, {
    provider,
    semanticWeight: 0.35
});
```

The adapter boundary makes external data disclosure an explicit host decision and keeps the
canonical Markdown/index implementation provider-independent.

### Experimental integration registry

Programmatic hosts can group approved semantic search and health adapters in a small,
vendor-neutral registry:

```js
import {
    createIntegrationRegistry,
    defineProjectIntegration
} from "@illodev/workfile/integrations";

const integrations = createIntegrationRegistry([
    defineProjectIntegration({
        id: "company.platform",
        semanticSearchProvider: provider,
        async healthCheck({ workspace, index }) {
            return [];
        }
    })
]);
```

The registry is accepted by the MCP server and doctor APIs. It is intentionally limited in
the current RC: vendor-specific issue trackers, deployment systems and credentials are not part of
the canonical package. The boundary can mature from real integrations without committing
the schema to GitHub, GitLab, Jira or a deployment provider.

## CI templates

CI files use the same managed-file contract and can be generated for GitHub Actions,
GitLab CI or a generic shell runner:

```bash
project ci sync --targets github,gitlab,generic
project ci check
```

Templates run both the workfile doctor and agent synchronization check against the pinned
Workfile version.

## Legacy migration

The v1 `.planning` system can be planned and applied with deterministic collision checks:

```bash
project migrate plan --source .planning
project migrate apply --source .planning --mode copy
project migrate apply --source .planning --mode move
```

Valid legacy cards and assets become canonical v2 Work records. Old proposals, changelogs,
learnings and malformed records are preserved under `.project/sources/legacy-planning/`
rather than being silently reinterpreted with an incompatible schema. Every applied
migration writes `.project/migrations/legacy-planning.json` with source, destination, digest
and result metadata.

## General CLI

```bash
project init
project schema --json
project doctor --json
project ui
```

Commands return stable machine-readable errors with `--json`. A stale revision exits with
code `3`; configuration errors exit with code `2`; validation and not-found errors exit
with code `1`. The complete command surface is documented in
[`docs/cli.md`](docs/cli.md).

## HTTP API

`workfile ui` starts the local server, normally at `http://127.0.0.1:4747`. The versioned
`/api/v2/*` surface covers the workspace, unified search, and every collection — cards,
docs, changelog (including release preview/assembly/render), memory lifecycle, agents and
CI sync. Managed record reads expose an `ETag`, writes accept `If-Match`, and errors use
stable codes. The endpoint reference lives in [`docs/http-api.md`](docs/http-api.md).

## Local UI

Navigation is a collapsible sidebar grouped by domain:

- **Work:** Explorer, Triage, Flow, Epics and a Gantt Timeline (status-colored bars,
  month scale, today marker).
- **Knowledge:** Docs (search, Markdown, metadata, freshness, scope, backlinks) and
  Memory (typed collections, lifecycle warnings, graduation and supersession).
- **Project:** History (fragments, releases, release preparation, rendered changelog
  preview) and Health.

Health issues can navigate to records in any domain. Runtime configuration drives card
areas, change vocabularies and memory collection statuses; these values are not compiled
into the views. File links open the local editor, or the repository web UI when the
server provides a `repoUrl` (as the hosted demo does).

| Explorer with the card drawer | Gantt timeline |
| --- | --- |
| ![Explorer with a card drawer open — claim, scope and metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illodev/workfile/main/.github/media/explorer.png) | ![Gantt timeline: month scale, status-colored bars and today marker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illodev/workfile/main/.github/media/timeline.png) |

| History with releases | Memory (dark theme) |
| --- | --- |
| ![History: change fragments, cut releases and release preparation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illodev/workfile/main/.github/media/history.png) | ![Memory: decisions, learnings, incidents and expiring context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/illodev/workfile/main/.github/media/memory-dark.png) |

## Development

The repository is developed with [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) (pinned via the
`packageManager` field; `corepack enable` picks it up automatically):

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run check
pnpm run smoke:package
node ./dist/bin/workfile.js mcp inspect --root ./test/fixtures/workspace --json
node ./dist/bin/workfile.js schema --root ./test/fixtures/workspace --json
node ./dist/bin/workfile.js doctor --root ./test/fixtures/workspace --json
node ./dist/bin/workfile.js ui --root ./test/fixtures/workspace
```

`pnpm run check` compiles the TypeScript runtime and declarations, checks the strict public
consumer contract, typechecks and bundles the React UI, and runs the complete test suite.
`pnpm run smoke:package` packs and installs the actual tarball in a temporary project before
exercising initialization, all four domains, MCP and the packaged UI — the smoke installs
with npm on purpose, exercising the npm consumer path.

`prepack` rebuilds the runtime declarations and UI so a future published package contains
only compiled runtime artifacts under `dist/`, never development TypeScript or a copied UI
source tree.

## Current guarantees

- restricted frontmatter codec with byte-stable scalar/list round trips;
- preservation of unknown frontmatter fields and body bytes;
- atomic file replacement, per-record locks and collision-safe ID reservations;
- SHA-256 revision tokens and stale-write rejection;
- atomic Work claims, transitions, archive and reopen operations;
- managed Docs, History fragments and typed Memory mutations;
- release assembly with canonical fragment consumption and derived rendering;
- configurable repository-safe paths and runtime vocabularies;
- common normalization, search, references and backlinks across all domains;
- health diagnostics for Work, Docs, History and Memory;
- compiled ESM and `.d.ts` declarations for the public package and subpath exports;
- executable packaged CLI/MCP binaries verified from a clean tarball installation;
- versioned API plus a compatibility adapter for the original board.

## Documents

- [`docs/getting-started.md`](docs/getting-started.md) — install, initialize and the
  daily loop.
- [`docs/cli.md`](docs/cli.md) — complete CLI reference for every module.
- [`docs/http-api.md`](docs/http-api.md) — endpoint reference, conventions and errors.
- [`docs/mcp.md`](docs/mcp.md) — MCP server contract: tools, resources, prompts.
- [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md) — threat model of the local server,
  request guard, asset handling and what is deliberately out of scope.
- [`docs/ui.md`](docs/ui.md) — the interface: its build, the zero-dependency
  guarantee and how the shadcn migration coexists with the design system.
- [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) — the normative protocol specification: data model,
  record contracts, revision semantics and the MCP integration contract.
